ashley.security: quick sync: after the RBAC tighten on webhook service accounts yesterday, our DAST scanner callbacks started failing and SAST started flagging generated client code. opening a thread to capture decisions and actions. :warning:
omar.eng: yep. scanner callbacks got 401/503s, retries overwhelmed the callback queue. logs show missing signature header.
noah-oncall: I paused the callback consumer to stop retries. what exact RBAC change happened?
maria.platform: we removed token:list and a couple of broad token permissions from webhook-sa to reduce scope for third-party connectors. intended, but we might have blocked the scanner token mint flow.
omar.eng: callback log snippet: ``503 downstream auth failure: missing X-Scanner-Signature header``. looks like the scanner couldn't sign callbacks because it couldn't mint the ephemeral token. ticket INC-5543 has the stack trace.
ashley.security: also SAST noise: generated scanner client includes a local-dev fallback that writes a plaintext placeholder key to /tmp. SAST flagged it as hardcoded secret (false positive for prod, but still not great).
devx: paste the snippet? maybe generator can be changed to keep key in memory or use KMS decrypt at runtime instead of file.
ashley.security: ``if (!process.env.SCAN_KEY) fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/scan_key', 'dev-key-placeholder')`` 3. trips detectors.
maria.platform: generator change sounds good. also consider marking generated/ files with a SAST metadata header that our scanner recognizes so we can avoid noisy alerts while still checking for real issues.
omar.eng: immediate mitigation plan: (1) temporarily rebind webhook-sa to restore token:mint permission, (2) change generator to decrypt into memory using KMS client, (3) add narrow SAST suppression for generated scanner clients with an audit link.
noah-oncall: I can put the temporary rebind in for 20 minutes and log it in the audit-bot.
sre-bot: deploy started: hotfix/rebind-webhook-sa -> staging (ci-2222).
audit-bot: RBAC CHANGE: user=noah-oncall ts=5543210025 action=add_binding reason="unblock scanner callbacks" revert_window=20m
devx: working on PR to update generator: title "infra: avoid disk writes for scanner keys, use KMS decrypt in-memory". adding unit and integration tests against staging scanner simulator.
omar.eng: for SAST suppression, propose adding this header at top of generated files: ``// SAST: auto-generated ignore-if-kms-link: https://go/repo/kms-guidance``. Then add an entry in `.sast-ignore` referencing the pattern and link.
ashley.security: agree but require a short manual review step for any generated-file suppression. include a TODO with GH issue link so we can track it.
maria.platform: long-term process fix: RBAC change playbook should include a preflight callback test for any SA removing token mint/list perms. I'll open a GH issue to add the simulator to the RBAC CI checks.
ashley.security: I'm recording action items in the incident ticket INC-5543: (A) devx/maria update generator PR, (B) omar add SAST header + `.sast-ignore` entry, (C) noah document temporary rebind and add preflight test to RBAC playbook.
noah-oncall: rolled the rebind back at 5543210100 after patch merged to staging. audit-bot entry updated with approver tag.
sre-bot: deploy succeeded: hotfix/rebind-webhook-sa -> staging (ci-2222). monitor 5m.
devx: PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/430. includes memory-only decrypt, tests, and changelog entry.
omar.eng: I'll add the `.sast-ignore` line and a short comment in the generator that explains the suppression, plus a pointer to the audit PR. We'll run a nightly full scan to confirm no regressions.
ashley.security: final notes for compliance: ensure KMS keys for scanner decrypt are in the rotation schedule, and add a checklist item to prevent any code path from writing plaintext key material to disk. adding to secure-sdlc board. :memo:
noah-oncall: closing the loop on incident scribe: INC-5543 updated with timeline, revert/restore entries, and links to PRs and audit logs. follow-up item added to weekly RBAC review.
ashley.security: thanks everyone, will do a short post-incident writeup with mitigation and prevention steps and link it to the RBAC playbook. :+1:
